title: At someone's home
goal: Visit a friend's family, be a good guest (and host), accept and decline food politely, ask whether something is OK, help out, stay the night — and talk about how things used to be.
intro:
Being invited home is the heart of Odia social life, and it comes with a script: shoes off at the door, *make yourself at home*, tea that you refuse once and then accept, a host who insists you eat *one more*, and an offer to help that the host will wave away.

This unit gives you both sides of that script. The grammar is what you need as a guest: polite **offers and refusals**, **should I…? / is it OK if…?** (ଖୋଲିବି କି?, ଶୋଇଲେ ଚଳିବ?) — and **used to** (-ଉଥିଲି), because sooner or later someone's mother will tell you what your friend *used to* do as a child.

vocab.en: to open; to take off (shoes, clothes)
vocab.note: ଜୋତା ଖୋଲିବା "to take off your shoes". Opposite of ପିନ୍ଧିବା.
Worn inside the house; hosts often keep a spare pair by the door.
Before a noun: ନିଜ ଘର "one's own home". ନିଜେ "oneself", ନିଜର "one's own" (standing alone).
Takes a plural verb: ଘରଲୋକ କେମିତି ଅଛନ୍ତି? "How is everyone at home?"
ସଙ୍କୋଚ କରିବା "to hold back, feel awkward". Hosts say ସଙ୍କୋଚ କର ନାହିଁ.
ଜୋର "force, strength".

vocab.en: to fill up; (stomach) to be full
vocab.note: ପେଟ ପୂରିଗଲା "I'm full" (lit. the stomach has filled).
ଆଦର କରିବା "to welcome warmly, make a fuss of".

vocab.en: to be OK, do, work; to get by
vocab.note: ଚଳିବ "that's fine, that'll do"; ଚଳିବ ନାହିଁ "that won't do". With -ଲେ: ଶୋଇଲେ ଚଳିବ? "is it OK if I sleep…?"
ଚାଲୁ "running, on". Switch off: ବନ୍ଦ କରିବା.
Most Odia homes have one. Never go in with shoes on.
The checked cotton towel used everywhere in Odisha. A thick towel is ଟାୱେଲ୍.
Usually switched on 10–15 minutes before a bath.
ବିଛଣା ତିଆରି କରିବା / ବିଛଣା ପକାଇବା "to make up a bed".
ମଶାରି ଟାଙ୍ଗିବା "to put up the mosquito net".

vocab.en: to hang (up); to put up (a net)
vocab.note: ଲୁଗା ଟାଙ୍ଗିବା "to hang up clothes".
ବାସନ ମାଜିବା "to do the dishes".

vocab.en: to wipe; to dry (with a cloth); to mop
vocab.note: ଘର ପୋଛିବା "to mop the floor".

vocab.en: to tidy up, arrange, put in order

vocab.note: Causative of ଶୁଖିବା "to get dry" (compare ଶୁଖିଲା "dry").
ପିଲାଦିନେ "as a child, in childhood".

vocab.en: earlier, before, in the old days
vocab.note: Pairs with -ଉଥିଲି: ଆଗେ ମୁଁ … କରୁଥିଲି "I used to…". Compare ଆଗରୁ "before (a point), already".
X-ର ଦେଖାଶୁଣା କରିବା "to look after X".

phrases.en: Come in, come in! (to a friend)
Make yourself at home. (lit. think of it like your own home)
Should I take my shoes off?
Don't be shy / don't hold back. (polite)

phrases.note: Odia often *eats* tea: ଚା ଖାଇବା is everyday speech; ଚା ପିଇବା is also correct.

phrases.en: Please don't go to so much trouble.
Have a little more! (insisting, to a friend)
I'm full, I can't manage any more.
How do I switch on the water heater?
Stay the night here tonight. (to a friend)
I'm fine sleeping on the sofa. (lit. if I sleep on the sofa it'll do)
Thank you for having me / for your hospitality.

grammar.title: 'Used to': the past habitual -ଉଥିଲି
grammar.body:
In unit 16 you met **-ଉଥିଲି** as 'was doing'. Its other big job is **used to / would** — things that kept happening in the past. It's how people talk about childhood, old homes and how things were: ପିଲାଦିନେ ମୁଁ ଅଜା ଘରେ ରହୁଥିଲି 'as a child I used to stay at my grandfather's'.

**Forms**: stem + **-ଉଥି-** + the past endings:
ମୁଁ ଯାଉଥିଲି *jauthili* — I used to go
ଆମେ / ତୁ ଯାଉଥିଲୁ *jauthilu*
ତୁମେ ଯାଉଥିଲ *jauthilô*
ଆପଣ / ସେ (resp.) / ସେମାନେ ଯାଉଥିଲେ *jauthile*
ସେ ଯାଉଥିଲା *jauthila*
Vowel stems work the same way: ଖାଉଥିଲି, ପିଉଥିଲି, ଦେଉଥିଲି, ଆସୁଥିଲି, କରୁଥିଲି.

**Negative**: put ନ before ଥିଲି, usually written as one word: **ଖାଉନଥିଲି** *khaunôthili* 'I didn't use to eat'.

**Time words** that go with it: **ଆଗେ** 'earlier, in the old days', **ପିଲାଦିନେ** 'as a child', **ସେତେବେଳେ** 'back then', **ସବୁ ରବିବାର** 'every Sunday'. Contrast with **ଏବେ** + simple present: ଆଗେ ମୁଁ ଚା ପିଉନଥିଲି, ଏବେ ଦିନକୁ ତିନି ଥର ପିଏ.

**The trap**: the simple past **-ଇଲି** is for *one* event: ଗତ ରବିବାର ପୁରୀ ଗଲି 'I went to Puri last Sunday'. **-ଉଥିଲି** is for what *kept* happening: ସବୁ ରବିବାର ପୁରୀ ଯାଉଥିଲି 'I used to go to Puri every Sunday'. Only context tells you whether -ଉଥିଲି means 'was doing' or 'used to do' — a time word like ଆଗେ or ପିଲାଦିନେ makes it clear.

examples.en: As a child I used to stay at my grandfather's.

examples.native: ଆଗେ ଆମେ ସବୁ ରବିବାର ପୁରୀ ଯାଉଥିଲୁ।
examples.roman: age ame sôbu rôbibarô Puri jauthilu.
examples.en: We used to go to Puri every Sunday.

examples.native: ଆଗେ ମୁଁ ଚା ପିଉନଥିଲି, ଏବେ ଦିନକୁ ତିନି ଥର ପିଏ।
examples.roman: age muṃ cha piunôthili, ebe dinôku tini thôrô pie.
examples.en: I didn't use to drink tea; now I have it three times a day.
Grandma used to make pitha for us.
You used to live in Cuttack, didn't you?

grammar.title: Offering, accepting and declining
grammar.body:
Odia hospitality follows a pattern: the host offers, the guest declines once or twice out of modesty, the host **insists** (ଜୋର କରେ), and the guest gives in. Knowing the lines on both sides makes you sound natural.

**Offering** — a future question: ଚା ଖାଇବ? (friend) / ଚା ଖାଇବେ? (polite) 'will you have tea?'; ଆଉ ଟିକେ ନେବେ? 'will you take a little more?'. A command with **ନା** at the end is warm and pushy in a nice way: ଆଉ ଟିକେ ନିଅ ନା! 'oh, have some more!'

**Accepting**: ହଉ, ଟିକେ ଦିଅ 'OK, just a little'; ଖାଲି … 'just …'; ଅବଶ୍ୟ 'sure'.

**Declining softly**: thank or praise first, then a reason. Useful lines: ଏତେ କଷ୍ଟ କରନ୍ତୁ ନାହିଁ 'don't go to such trouble'; ପେଟ ପୂରିଗଲା 'I'm full'; ବହୁତ ହେଲା 'that's plenty'; ଆଉ ପାରିବି ନାହିଁ 'I can't manage more'; ଆଜି ନୁହେଁ, ଆଉ ଦିନେ 'not today, another time'. A bare ନା sounds cold — say ନା ନା with a smile.

**Don't …!** — negative commands, used constantly by hosts:
polite: **-ନ୍ତୁ ନାହିଁ** — ସଙ୍କୋଚ କରନ୍ତୁ ନାହିଁ
familiar: **-ଅ ନାହିଁ** — ଲାଜ କର ନାହିଁ, ଆଉ ଦିଅ ନାହିଁ
The future + ନାହିଁ is gentler: ମନା କରିବ ନାହିଁ 'you won't say no now'.

**Trap**: in Odia, tea is often *eaten* — ଚା ଖାଇବା. It isn't a mistake; it's how most people say it.

examples.native: ଲାଜ କର ନାହିଁ, ଆଉ ଗୋଟିଏ ପିଠା ନିଅ।
examples.roman: lajô kôrô nahiṃ, au goṭie piṭha niô.
examples.en: Don't be shy, have another pitha.

examples.native: ଧନ୍ୟବାଦ ମାଉସୀ, ଆଜି ନୁହେଁ, ଆଉ ଦିନେ।
examples.roman: dhônnyôbadô mausi, aji nuheṃ, au dine.
examples.en: Thank you, auntie — not today, another time.

grammar.title: Should I…? Is it OK if…?
grammar.body:
As a guest you are always checking: should I take my shoes off? can I have a bath? is it OK if I sleep here? Four patterns cover it:

**Shall I / should I?** — the ମୁଁ-future, often with **କି**: ଜୋତା ଖୋଲିବି କି? 'should I take my shoes off?' Add **ଦେବା** to offer to do something *for* someone: ମୁଁ ବାସନ ମାଜି**ଦେବି**? 'shall I do the dishes (for you)?'

**Do I have to?** — **-ବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବ କି?**: ଜୋତା ଖୋଲିବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବ କି? 'do I have to take my shoes off?'

**Is it OK if…?** — the **-ଲେ** ('if') form + **ଚଳିବ?** 'will it do?': ମୁଁ ଏଠି ଶୋଇଲେ ଚଳିବ? 'is it OK if I sleep here?'. Answers: ହଁ, ଚଳିବ 'sure, that's fine' / ନା, ଚଳିବ ନାହିଁ 'no, that's not OK'. ଚଳିବ on its own — 'that works, that'll do' — is one of the most useful words in Odia.

**May I?** — **-ଇପାରେ କି?** (unit 18): ମୁଁ ଗାଧୋଇପାରେ କି? 'may I have a bath?'

**What should I do?** — ମୁଁ କ'ଣ କରିବି?; for advice, **-ବା ଉଚିତ** (unit 9): ଠାକୁର ଘରକୁ ଜୋତା ପିନ୍ଧି ଯିବା ଉଚିତ ନୁହେଁ 'you shouldn't go into the prayer room in shoes'.

**Trap**: the ending tells you *who* — ଖୋଲିବି? 'shall *I* take them off?', but ଖୋଲିବେ? 'will *you* take them off?' (a polite request to someone else).

examples.en: Should I leave my shoes outside?
Where shall I put the towel?
Is it OK if I come a bit late?

examples.native: ମୁଁ ଏଠି ଫୋନ ଚାର୍ଜ କରିପାରେ କି?
examples.roman: muṃ eṭhi phonô charj kôripare ki?
examples.en: May I charge my phone here?

dialogue.title: Dinner at Bapi's in Cuttack
dialogue.setting: Sam visits his friend Bapi's family in Cuttack for the first time, with a box of sweets.

lines.speaker: Bapi
lines.native: ଆସ ଆସ, ସାମ୍! ଘର ଖୋଜିବାକୁ ଅସୁବିଧା ହେଲା ନାହିଁ ତ?
lines.roman: asô asô, Sam! ghôrô khojibaku ôsubidha hela nahiṃ tô?
lines.en: Come in, come in, Sam! You didn't have trouble finding the house, did you?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ଟିକେ ହେଲା, ଗୁଗୁଲ୍ ମ୍ୟାପ୍ ମୋତେ ସବୁ ଗଳିରେ ବୁଲାଇଲା! ଜୋତା ଏଠି ଖୋଲିବି କି?
lines.roman: ṭike hela, Gugul myap mote sôbu gôḷire bulaila! jota eṭhi kholibi ki?
lines.en: A bit — Google Maps took me down every lane in town! Should I take my shoes off here?

lines.speaker: Bapi
lines.native: ହଁ, ସେଠି ଚପଲ ଅଛି, ପିନ୍ଧିନିଅ। ବୋଉ, ସାମ୍ ଆସିଗଲା!
lines.roman: hôṃ, seṭhi chôpôlô ôchhi, pindhiniô. bou, Sam asigôla!
lines.en: Yes, there are slippers there, put them on. Mum, Sam's here!

lines.speaker: Bapi's mum
lines.native: ଆସ ବାପା, ବସ। ନିଜ ଘର ପରି ଭାବ, ସଙ୍କୋଚ କର ନାହିଁ।
lines.roman: asô bapa, bôsô. nijô ghôrô pôri bhabô, sôṅkochô kôrô nahiṃ.
lines.en: Come, dear, sit down. Make yourself at home, don't be shy.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ନମସ୍କାର ମାଉସୀ। ଏଇ ମିଠା ଆପଣଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ — ପାହାଳର ରସଗୋଲା।
lines.roman: nômôskarô mausi. ei miṭha apôṇôṅkô paiṃ — Pahaḷôrô rôsôgola.
lines.en: Hello, auntie. These sweets are for you — rasagolas from Pahala.

lines.speaker: Bapi's mum
lines.native: ଆରେ, ଏସବୁ କାହିଁକି ଆଣିଲ? ଚା ଖାଇବ ନା କଫି?
lines.roman: are, esôbu kahiṃki aṇilô? cha khaibô na kôphi?
lines.en: Oh, why did you bring all this? Tea or coffee?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ଏତେ କଷ୍ଟ କରନ୍ତୁ ନାହିଁ, ମାଉସୀ। ଖାଲି ପାଣି ଚଳିବ।
lines.roman: ete kôsṭô kôrôntu nahiṃ, mausi. khali paṇi chôḷibô.
lines.en: Please don't go to any trouble, auntie. Just water is fine.

lines.speaker: Bapi
lines.native: ସେ ମିଛ କହୁଛି, ବୋଉ। ସେ ଦିନକୁ ପାଞ୍ଚ କପ୍ ଚା ପିଏ!
lines.roman: se michhô kôhuchhi, bou. se dinôku pañchô kôp cha pie!
lines.en: He's lying, Mum. He drinks five cups of tea a day!

lines.speaker: Bapi's mum
lines.native: ତେବେ ଚା ଆଉ ପିଠା ଆଣୁଛି। ପିଲାଦିନେ ବାପି ବି ଏମିତି ଲାଜ କରୁଥିଲା।
lines.roman: tebe cha au piṭha aṇuchhi. piladine Bapi bi emiti lajô kôruthila.
lines.en: Then I'm bringing tea and pitha. Bapi used to be shy like this as a little boy, too.

lines.speaker: Bapi's mum
lines.native: ଆଜି ରାତି ଏଠି ରହିଯାଅ। ବାହାରେ ବର୍ଷା ହେଉଛି।
lines.roman: aji rati eṭhi rôhijaô. bahare bôrsa heuchhi.
lines.en: Stay the night tonight. It's raining outside.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ସତରେ? ଅସୁବିଧା ନ ହେଲେ… ମୁଁ ସୋଫାରେ ଶୋଇଯିବି।
lines.roman: sôtôre? ôsubidha nô hele… muṃ sophare soijibi.
lines.en: Really? If it's no trouble… I'll sleep on the sofa.

lines.speaker: Bapi
lines.native: ସୋଫା କାହିଁକି? ମୋ କୋଠରୀରେ ବିଛଣା ଅଛି। କେବଳ ମଶାରି ଟାଙ୍ଗିବାକୁ ଭୁଲିବ ନାହିଁ — କଟକ ମଶା ପ୍ରସିଦ୍ଧ!
lines.roman: sopha kahiṃki? mo koṭhôrire bichhôṇa ôchhi. kebôḷô môsari ṭaṅgibaku bhulibô nahiṃ — Kôṭôkô môsa prôsiddhô!
lines.en: Why the sofa? There's a bed in my room. Just don't forget to put up the mosquito net — Cuttack's mosquitoes are famous!

culture: Odisha takes hospitality seriously — guests are traditionally treated like gods. Bring something when you visit: a box of sweets (rasagola from **Pahala**, *chhena poda*, or anything from a good sweet shop) or fruit. Shoes come off at the door, and the prayer room (**ଠାକୁର ଘର**) and often the kitchen are off-limits unless you are invited in. Call a friend's parents **ମାଉସୀ** (auntie) and **ମଉସା** (uncle) and use ଆପଣ with them; don't be surprised when an older woman calls a young man **ବାପା** or **ବାପୁ** and a young woman **ମା** — it's an endearment, like 'dear'. Food will be offered again and again: refusing once is good manners, but refusing everything is not. To stop, cover your plate with your hand and say **ପେଟ ପୂରିଗଲା**. Offer to help with the dishes — you will probably be told **ନା ନା, ତୁମେ ଅତିଥି** — and at least carry your own plate to the sink. When you leave, say **ଆସୁଛି** ('I'm coming'), never ଯାଉଛି ('I'm going'), which sounds final.

tip.title: Welcome lines
tip.body:
- Hosts double the welcome: **ଆସ ଆସ, ବସ** (to a friend) / **ଆସନ୍ତୁ, ବସନ୍ତୁ** (polite).
- Shoes come off at the door; slippers (**ଚପଲ**) are often offered.
- Call a friend's parents **ମାଉସୀ** and **ମଉସା** (auntie, uncle) and use ଆପଣ with them.

sentences.en: Take your shoes off here and put on some slippers.
Please make yourself comfortable on the sofa.
How is everyone at home?

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ନିଜ ଘରେ ବି ଏମିତି ଆରାମରେ ବସେ ନାହିଁ!
sentences.roman: muṃ nijô ghôre bi emiti aramôre bôse nahiṃ!
sentences.en: I don't even sit this comfortably at my own place!
My family want to meet you.
The door's open, come on in.
Shall I open the window for you?
Relax, I'll get you some water.

tip.title: Offers and polite refusals
tip.body:
- Offer with a future question: ଚା **ଖାଇବ**? (friend) / **ଖାଇବେ**? (polite).
- Say *don't* with **-ଅ ନାହିଁ** (friend: ଲାଜ କର ନାହିଁ) or **-ନ୍ତୁ ନାହିଁ** (polite: ଜୋର କରନ୍ତୁ ନାହିଁ).
- Decline softly: ନା ନା, **ପେଟ ପୂରିଗଲା** / **ଏତେ କଷ୍ଟ କରନ୍ତୁ ନାହିଁ**. Refuse once — the host will insist.

sentences.en: Will you have a couple of pitha?
Will you have a little more rice? (polite)

sentences.native: ସଙ୍କୋଚ କର ନାହିଁ, ପେଟ ପୂରା ଖାଅ।
sentences.roman: sôṅkochô kôrô nahiṃ, peṭô pura khaô.
sentences.en: Don't hold back — eat your fill.

sentences.native: ନା ନା, ଆଉ ଦିଅ ନାହିଁ, ପେଟ ପୂରିଗଲା।
sentences.roman: na na, au diô nahiṃ, peṭô purigôla.
sentences.en: No no, don't give me any more — I'm full.

sentences.native: ମାଉସୀ ଜୋର କଲେ, ତେଣୁ ମୁଁ ଆଉ ଦୁଇଟା ରସଗୋଲା ଖାଇଲି।
sentences.roman: mausi jorô kôle, teṇu muṃ au duiṭa rôsôgola khaili.
sentences.en: Auntie insisted, so I ate two more rasagolas.

sentences.native: ଏତେ ଜୋର କରନ୍ତୁ ନାହିଁ, ମୁଁ ସତରେ ଖାଇପାରିବି ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: ete jorô kôrôntu nahiṃ, muṃ sôtôre khaiparibi nahiṃ.
sentences.en: Please don't insist so much — I really can't eat any more.
OK, just half a glass.
Some more tea?

sentences.native: ଲାଜ କର ନାହିଁ, ଯାହା ଦରକାର କୁହ।
sentences.roman: lajô kôrô nahiṃ, jaha dôrôkarô kuhô.
sentences.en: Don't be shy — tell me whatever you need.

tip.title: Should I…? Is it OK if…?
tip.body:
- Shall I? — ମୁଁ-future (+ **କି**): ଜୋତା **ଖୋଲିବି କି**?
- Is it OK if…? — **-ଲେ** + **ଚଳିବ?**: ଏଠି **ବସିଲେ ଚଳିବ**? Answer: ହଁ, ଚଳିବ / ନା, ଚଳିବ ନାହିଁ.
- Do I have to? — **-ବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବ କି?**
- May I? — **-ଇପାରେ କି?**

sentences.en: May I have a bath?
Where are the towel and soap?
Is it OK if I sit here?
Yes, of course, that's fine — sit.
Shall I switch the water heater on for you?
Is it OK if I take photos in the prayer room?

sentences.native: ନା, ସେଠି ଫଟୋ ନେବା ଚଳିବ ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: na, seṭhi phôṭo neba chôḷibô nahiṃ.
sentences.en: No, taking photos in there isn't OK.

sentences.native: ଠାକୁର ଘରକୁ ଜୋତା ପିନ୍ଧି ଯିବା ଉଚିତ ନୁହେଁ।
sentences.roman: ṭhakurô ghôrôku jota pindhi jiba uchitô nuheṃ.
sentences.en: You shouldn't go into the prayer room with shoes on.
Do I have to take my shoes off?
I've made up a bed for you.
Could I have another pillow?

sentences.native: ରାତିରେ ଥଣ୍ଡା ହେଲେ ଏଇ ଚଦର ନିଅ।
sentences.roman: ratire thôṇḍa hele ei chôdôrô niô.
sentences.en: If it gets cold at night, take this sheet.
There are lots of mosquitoes here — I'll put up the net for you.
I'm fine sleeping on the floor, too.
What time do you get up in the morning?

sentences.native: ବାହାରେ ବର୍ଷା ହେଉଛି, ଆଜି ଆଉ ଯାଅ ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: bahare bôrsa heuchhi, aji au jaô nahiṃ.
sentences.en: It's raining outside — don't go tonight.

sentences.native: କାଲି ସକାଳେ ବାପା ତୁମକୁ ଷ୍ଟେସନରେ ଛାଡ଼ିଦେବେ।
sentences.roman: kali sôkaḷe bapa tumôku sṭesônôre chhaṛidebe.
sentences.en: Dad will drop you at the station tomorrow morning.

tip.title: Offering to help: -ଇଦେବି?
tip.body:
- ମୁଁ-future + **ଦେବା** offers to do something *for* someone: ପୋଛି**ଦେବି**? 'shall I wipe it (for you)?'
- The host will say **ନା ନା, ଛାଡ଼** — offer once more.
- To insist: ମୋତେ **…-ବାକୁ ଦିଅ** 'let me…': ମୋତେ ମାଜିବାକୁ ଦିଅ.

sentences.en: Shall I wipe the table?
No no, leave it — you're a guest.

sentences.native: ମୋତେ ବାସନ ମାଜିବାକୁ ଦିଅ, ମୋର ଅଭ୍ୟାସ ଅଛି।
sentences.roman: mote basônô majibaku diô, morô ôbbhyasô ôchhi.
sentences.en: Let me do the dishes — I'm used to it.
Shall I hang the clothes out to dry on the veranda?
I'll tidy my own bed.
You wash the dishes, I'll dry them.

sentences.native: ମାଉସୀ, ମୁଁ ଆପଣଙ୍କୁ ଟିକେ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ କରିଦେବି?
sentences.roman: mausi, muṃ apôṇôṅku ṭike sahajjyô kôridebi?
sentences.en: Auntie, shall I give you a hand?
Will you chop the vegetables for me?

tip.title: Used to: -ଉଥିଲି
tip.body:
- Past habits: stem + **-ଉଥିଲି**: ପିଲାଦିନେ ମୁଁ ଖେଳ**ଉଥିଲି** 'as a kid I used to play'.
- Endings: -ଉଥିଲି (I), -ଉଥିଲୁ (we), -ଉଥିଲ (you), -ଉଥିଲେ (polite / they), -ଉଥିଲା (he, she).
- Negative: **-ଉନଥିଲି** 'I didn't use to'.
- One event is simple past: ଗଲି; a repeated one is ଯାଉଥିଲି.

sentences.native: ପିଲାଦିନେ ମୁଁ ଗରମ ଛୁଟିରେ ଅଜା ଘରକୁ ଯାଉଥିଲି।
sentences.roman: piladine muṃ gôrômô chhuṭire ôja ghôrôku jauthili.
sentences.en: As a kid I used to go to my grandpa's in the summer holidays.
Grandma used to look after us.

sentences.native: ଆଗେ ମୁଁ ମାଛ ଖାଉନଥିଲି, ଏବେ ଭଲ ପାଏ।
sentences.roman: age muṃ machhô khaunôthili, ebe bhôlô pae.
sentences.en: I didn't use to eat fish — now I love it.
As kids we used to play outside in the evenings.

sentences.native: ତୁମେ ଆଗେ ଏତେ ଚା ପିଉଥିଲ କି?
sentences.roman: tume age ete cha piuthilô ki?
sentences.en: Did you use to drink this much tea before?

sentences.native: ବାପା ଆଗେ ଅଫିସ୍ ଚାଲି ଚାଲି ଯାଉଥିଲେ।
sentences.roman: bapa age ôphis chali chali jauthile.
sentences.en: Dad used to walk to the office.

sentences.native: ଏ ଘରେ ଆଗେ ମୋ ମାମୁଁ ରହୁଥିଲେ।
sentences.roman: e ghôre age mo mamuṃ rôhuthile.
sentences.en: My uncle used to live in this house.

sentences.native: ଆପଣଙ୍କ ଆଦର ମୋର ସବୁଦିନ ମନେ ରହିବ।
sentences.roman: apôṇôṅkô adôrô morô sôbudinô mône rôhibô.
sentences.en: I'll always remember how welcome you made me feel.
